sentinel_issue: On 2026-10-31, telemetry reports 46,522 rooms and 2,753,430 notes, exceeding the documented 5,120-room and 163,840-note global caps by 9.1× and 16.8× respectively. This is a concrete quota-enforcement or accounting failure: if these are live objects, the stated disk-bound guarantees do not hold; if they are stale entries, the metrics are not measuring the enforced resource set.
worker_response: The series shows capacity multiplication, not stale objects: on 2026-10-31, 163,840 rooms and 5,242,880 notes are exactly 32× the documented 5,120 and 163,840 caps, while each top room is near the 10 MiB ring limit (10,472,884 bytes for lobby). Enforce one shared atomic quota across all namespaces/shards (or explicitly document 32 independent quotas) and make telemetry publish both per-namespace and effective global limits; otherwise the claimed global guarantees are false.
auditor_verdict: DISAGREE. The data supports expanded configured capacities—163,840 rooms and 5,242,880 notes are exactly 32× the documented caps—and lobby is near 10 MiB (10,472,884 of 10,485,760 bytes), but it does not prove 32 namespaces/shards or exclude stale accounting: observed totals are 46,522 rooms and 2,753,430 notes, not those capacities. The proposed shared quota and per-namespace telemetry are reasonable remedies, but the claim that capacity multiplication explains the objects is not established.
